Your first long ruck

Build a long outing you can actually repeat, rather than making your first distance a survival exercise.

Practical training guide

Start from a session you know

Use the longest recent outing that felt manageable and left you able to get on with your next day. Record elapsed time, pack mass and the route. If you are new, an unloaded walk is a perfectly good baseline.

A simple progression

  1. Repeat the baseline until it feels familiar.
  2. Add a little time to one outing while keeping weight, surface and pace familiar.
  3. Keep the other sessions easy and repeat the new outing before increasing it again.
  4. If recovery or foot comfort worsens, go back to the previous session.

Plan the middle of the route

Pick a route with clear exit options, water and toilet access. Tell someone the plan if heading somewhere remote. A loop with safe ways to shorten it is useful when learning your limits.

The week before

Do not squeeze a new personal best into the last few days. Use a familiar load, food and footwear. Allow recovery before a bigger outing.

Review the result

Note elapsed time, stops, pack mass, foot problems and how you feel the next day. A finish is useful information, not automatic permission to increase everything.
